analyst.summary: BHEL's order book (Rs 2.4-2.6 lakh crore, +27% YoY) is a legitimate, well-documented beneficiary of India's 80 GW+ coal-capacity revival and a genuinely diversifying (nuclear/rail/transmission/defence, ~40% of book) franchise, with tangible evidence of improved bidding economics on newer contracts. But profitability, while genuinely inflecting (FY26 net profit tripled to Rs 1,600 cr, ROE to 6%/ROCE to 9%, both five-year highs), remains thin and volatile -- Q1 FY27's EBITDA margin fell straight back to ~7% from Q4 FY26's 14.2%, management guides to merely hold ~10.7% margin through FY28, and the quality-score percentile of 3.1 reflects a still-structural pattern of poor capital efficiency that two good quarters have not overturned. The quant snapshot's 94.7x PE/0.2% ROE is meaningfully stale (a trailing window still carrying Q1 FY26's loss); corrected current figures are ~60.4x trailing PE and 5.6-5.8x book against screener.in -- still extreme for a 6% ROE business. The stock has already re-rated +105% off its August-2025 low to an all-time high, and sell-side is genuinely split (Macquarie/CLSA targets 30%+ below CMP vs ICICI Sec/IIFL/360 ONE 15-20% above). Net call: Sell -- take the re-rating gain rather than underwrite further multiple expansion on a fragile, not-yet-proven margin recovery, while flagging this as a real judgment call given the underlying order-flow thesis is genuinely intact.
